## Objective

Support complete new setup and explicit prior-edition module adoption with preservation and recovery.

## Scope

- Add the learning setup edition without changing earlier editions
- Check module and dependency compatibility
- Include learning in new and first-time existing setup
- Add explicitly selected prior-edition module adoption
- Record and recover module adoption in existing setup state

## Entry conditions

- The module and shared memory interface are defined.

## Exit criteria

- v7 setup, compatibility, scoped prior-edition adoption and receipt continuation are implemented.

## Risks

- Preserve v1-v6 semantics, existing memory bindings and whole customized packages.

### Risks

- Changing the latest-edition constant alone would accidentally alter v6 behavior.

### Acceptance criteria

- v7 includes learning; memory semantics remain v5-v7 and automatic-capture semantics remain v6-v7.
- v1-v6 validation, role casing, licensing, prior source inventories and ordinary-rerun meaning remain intact.
- Required learning resources and the compatibility inventory are checked before a successful new module setup.

### Planned verification

- Review every SETUP_CONTRACT equality and edition membership branch.
- Add and run minimal explicit v1-v6/v7 edition regression cases, retaining older fixtures while updating latest-edition expectations; reject missing or unsafe starter assets before writes.

## TASK-010 - Add explicitly selected prior-edition module adoption

Add prepare-existing --adopt-module what-did-you-learn for an exact already-initialized destination, using a confined module/dependency manifest and the current Template source.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |

| Dependencies | TASK-009 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-09T05:11:45.851912Z |

### Risks

- None

### Acceptance criteria

- Only a valid completed base setup may start module adoption; recover an unfinished base setup first.
- A compatible prior-edition fixture acquires learning while base setup_contract, original source/owned/preserved inventories and history remain unchanged.
- Ordinary reruns acquire no new edition; repeated equivalent module requests verify the same operation without duplicate registration.
- The selected manifest may refresh a complete unchanged receipt-owned dependency package as a whole when explicitly included; matching filenames alone grant no refresh authority.
- Customized/incomplete dependencies remain untouched and get a precise scoped adoption requirement. Existing config, capture off and notes remain unchanged.
- A v1-v4 project without memory receives only the selected missing empty memory capability with new local provenance; later memory fields are not inserted into its original base inventory.
- Existing legacy role-layout gates remain in force and no product is selected merely by registration.

### Planned verification

- Exercise a genuine v6 receipt with old completed assets, a pre-memory receipt with compatible current role proof, and a custom-package conflict.
- Compare before/after base receipt fields and hash the exact selected adoption manifest.

## TASK-011 - Record and recover module adoption in existing setup state

Extend the existing setup receipt with a validated module_adoptions collection and checked continuation while retaining its original base record and content-hash history.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |

| Dependencies | TASK-010 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-09T05:11:59.327497Z |

### Risks

- No second setup ledger or blanket migration; extend the existing receipt validator deliberately.

### Acceptance criteria

- Each selected module operation records identity, module version, Template hashes, exact targets, before/after bytes, adopted/preserved/skipped decisions, checks and capability status.
- Existing archive_record preserves each earlier receipt and base setup fields retain their original meaning.
- The existing project and Template locks protect the adoption; retry accepts only frozen sources and expected before/after bytes.
- Interrupted or partially committed work returns its actual boundary; changed source, identity, destination or competing writer prevents unsafe replay.
- Completed reruns retain normal subsequent project edits and never become an implicit refresh.

### Planned verification

- Inject interruption before first publication, between files and before/after receipt verification; resume the exact operation.
- Test source drift, concurrent edits, active lock, invalid nested provenance and retained old-receipt validation.
